paragraphs: We were founded on the belief that engineered cells will be one of the most important transformations in medicine over the next several decades. The burden of diseases that can be addressed at their root cause through engineered cells is significant. We view engineered cells as having the potential to be as therapeutically disruptive as biologic drugs to clinical practice, enabling us to repair cells in the body when possible and replace them when needed. We have developed ex vivo and in vivo cell engineering platforms to revolutionize treatment across a broad array of therapeutic areas with unmet treatment needs, including type 1 diabetes, oncology, and B cell mediated autoimmune diseases.

For our ex vivo platform, we have made focused investments in our hypoimmune platform technology, which we refer to as our HIP technology, with the twin goals of engineering allogeneic cells that can "hide" from the patient's immune system to overcome the fundamental challenge of immune rejection and cell persistence and that we can manufacture at scale. A successful therapeutic requires cells that can engraft, function, and persist in the body, and we believe our approach can unlock a wave of disruptive therapeutics, starting in type 1 diabetes. For in vivo therapies that aim to repair or control genes in the body, a successful product candidate requires both gene modification and in vivo delivery of the therapeutic payload. Our initial focus is on cell-specific delivery of genetic payloads, known as chimeric antigen receptors (CARs), to a patient's T cells, resulting in the generation and proliferation of CAR T cells, which have been shown to deplete a patient's disease-causing B cells.

We are currently focused on advancing two distinct therapeutics, each of which leverages one of these platform technologies. SC451 is our HIP-edited product candidate for the treatment of type 1 diabetes. SG293 is our in vivo CAR T product candidate for the treatment of B cell malignancies and B cell mediated autoimmune diseases.

• Type 1 Diabetes: Almost ten million people suffer from type 1 diabetes (T1D) worldwide, and there has been limited progress in treatments for this disease since the advent of insulin injections over 100 years ago. We are developing SC451, a HIP-modified, stem cell-derived pancreatic islet cell therapy, for the treatment of T1D. The goal of this therapy is euglycemia, or normal blood glucose, without the need for exogenous insulin injections or immunosuppression. Through a first-in-human investigator-sponsored study (IST), we have shown that UP421, an allogeneic, primary islet cell therapy engineered with our HIP technology, can survive and function for twelve months post-transplant in a patient with T1D without the need for immunosuppression. We have incorporated this HIP technology into a more scalable manufacturing platform with SC451 and expect to file an investigational new drug application (IND) as well as begin a Phase 1 clinical trial for this therapy as early as this year.

• In vivo CAR T cells: Using our fusogen platform, which enables cell-specific, in vivo delivery of various payloads, we are developing SG293, a CD8-targeted fusosome. SG293 delivers genetic material to CD8+ T cells, which enables them to become CD19-targeting CAR T cells while avoiding potentially problematic delivery to tissues such as the liver and gonads. In vivo CAR T cells have the potential to provide the clinical benefit of autologous, ex vivo manufactured CAR T cells while avoiding the need for lymphodepleting chemotherapy as well as significant complexity and delays related to manufacturing. SG293 builds on data from our prior lead in vivo CAR T product candidate, SG299. We plan to develop SG293 in a range of B cell cancers and B cell mediated autoimmune diseases and expect to generate initial clinical data as early as this year.

SC451 is our lead program for T1D. T1D is a disease in which the patient's immune system attacks and kills the patient's pancreatic beta cells, the only cells in the human body that make insulin, leading to a complete loss of insulin production in affected individuals. Insulin is essential for normal cellular metabolism, and prior to the discovery of insulin replacement therapy over 100 years ago, a person typically died within months of diagnosis. Insulin therapy has meaningfully improved patient outcomes, but even with state-of-the-art medical care and technology and glucose control, a person with T1D will live approximately a decade less than somebody without the disease and have a significant treatment burden for life. In contrast, our goal is to develop a one-time treatment that leads to normal blood glucose with no insulin injections and no immunosuppression, in an effort to restore the patient to a life similar to that from before the T1D diagnosis. Pancreatic islets are comprised of pancreatic beta cells and other endocrine cells. Scientists have shown that transplanted pancreatic islets can allow patients to come off insulin and maintain normal blood glucose. These islets can be obtained from deceased donors or derived from stem cells. However, the impact of these therapies has been limited, as patients must remain on life-long systemic immunosuppression to prevent the patient's immune system from rejecting these transplanted cells. The potential complications of immunosuppression, which include increased susceptibility to infection, heightened cancer risk, cardiovascular disease, metabolic syndrome, chronic kidney disease, and osteoporosis, outweigh the potential benefits of these treatments in most patients.

Our HIP technology is designed to hide transplanted cells from immune recognition and rejection. In addition to extensive pre-clinical testing, the ability of our HIP technology to hide transplanted pancreatic islets from immune recognition and rejection has been demonstrated in a human.

In December 2024, UP421, a HIP-modified allogeneic primary islet cell therapy, was transplanted into a patient with T1D in an IST conducted at Uppsala University Hospital. This study evaluates the safety of UP421 when transplanted intramuscularly into a patient with T1D. Secondary endpoints include immune evasion, non-fasting C-peptide concentrations in peripheral blood, C-peptide response to a mixed meal tolerance test (MMTT), and graft survival assessed by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and Positron Emission Tomography (PET/MRI). Pancreatic beta cells produce pro-insulin, which is cleaved and secreted as insulin and C-peptide in a 1:1 ratio, making C-peptide a well-established biomarker of endogenous insulin production. The 42-year-old recipient, who had been living with T1D for over 30 years, received a single transplant of UP421 into the muscle of the forearm. The transplantation was performed without immunosuppression, steroids, or any supportive medication to facilitate allogeneic cell survival. As a first-in-human study, the primary endpoint was safety, and the dose was approximately 7% of islet cells that would typically be needed for insulin independence.

In January 2025, we announced positive results from the IST at four weeks after cell transplantation, which demonstrated the survival and function of pancreatic beta cells as measured by the presence of circulating C-peptide. In September 2025, 12-week data from the IST were published in The New England Journal of Medicine. In addition, we recently reported that at 12 months following transplantation, the UP421 first-in-human study continues to demonstrate durable safety, survival, and function of the transplanted HIP-modified primary islet cells. The primary endpoint of safety was achieved, with no drug product-related adverse events reported. Prior to transplant, C-peptide levels were undetectable both in the non-fasting state and in response to an MMTT. Results of the study through twelve months following transplantation demonstrate the survival and function of pancreatic beta cells as measured by the presence of circulating C-peptide. C-peptide levels also increased with an MMTT during testing at these timepoints, consistent with insulin secretion in response to a meal. PET/MRI imaging results at 12 weeks and 12 months are consistent with pancreatic beta cell survival and function in the forearm muscle of the patient.

The UP421 drug product contains a mixture of islet cell populations: wild-type (WT) islet cells expressing HLA class I and class II, double knockout (DKO) islet cells with HLA class I and class II eliminated, and HIP islet cells with both HLA class I and class II eliminated plus CD47 overexpression. We performed assays testing the patient's various immune cell responses to these different populations of cells in the drug product. Consistent with expectations post-transplantation of allogeneic tissue, WT islet cells triggered a robust immune response with T cell-mediated killing and development of donor-specific antibodies. DKO islet cells, while avoiding T cell activation and antibody responses, were rapidly eliminated by natural killer (NK) cells. In contrast, HIP islet cells demonstrated comprehensive immune evasion, with no evidence of T cell activation, donor-specific antibody development, or NK cell-mediated killing. These distinct immune responses were further validated in whole blood assays, in which HIP islet cells survived exposure to the patient's peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) while both WT and DKO islet cells were eliminated. These in vitro assay results are consistent throughout the 52 weeks of the study to date. For additional information on the genetic modifications discussed above, see the sections titled "Background on Immunological Barriers to ex vivo Therapies and Current Limitations," "Our Solution – Hypoimmune Technology," and "Designing Hypoimmune Cells" below.

To our knowledge, this study is the first example of successful transplantation with no immunosuppression into a person with an intact immune system to demonstrate survival and function of allogeneic cells. We believe these results with HIP-modified cells represent a significant milestone for the field of cell therapy. These cells not only had to overcome the typical rejection of allogeneic cells, they also needed to overcome the pre-existing autoimmune response to pancreatic beta cells. The results are a key landmark in our effort to develop SC451, our HIP modified stem cell-derived pancreatic islet cell product candidate, as an off-the-shelf cell therapy for patients with T1D.

UP421 is derived from the cells of a deceased donor. In contrast, SC451 is derived from stem cells and is therefore more amenable to commercial scale. We have made meaningful progress with SC451 over the past year. We have completed manufacture of our gene-modified stem cell master cell bank, begun tech transfer of our Phase 1 manufacturing process to our partner contract manufacturers, continued our necessary preclinical tests, and met with regulators in various parts of the world. We expect to submit an IND for SC451 and begin our Phase 1 trial as early as this year.

With respect to our in vivo cell engineering research efforts, we have advanced from our earlier SG299 in vivo CAR T candidate to an improved next-generation product candidate, SG293, both of which use our proprietary fusogen-based delivery platform. In January 2026, we shared data from a preclinical study using a surrogate for SG293 that delivers a CD20 CAR capable of targeting non-human primate (NHP) B cells in cynomolgus macaques. No lymphodepletion was administered to the NHPs in this study. A single intravenous injection of the SG293 surrogate to these NHPs resulted in robust in vivo generation of CAR T cells and deep B cell depletion in the peripheral blood and lymph nodes. The B cell depletion was further confirmed by lymph node biopsies showing clearance of B cells as well as by "reset" of the NHPs' B cell repertoire toward naïve B cells. We believe that deep B cell depletion in this preclinical model is the most significant biomarker for potential efficacy in patients with B cell cancers and B cell mediated autoimmune diseases. Separately, in vitro studies using SG293 have shown selective gene delivery to CD8+ T cells with minimal or undetectable off-target transduction in tissues such as the liver and gonadal tissue, supporting the specificity of SG293. We continue to evaluate SG293 preclinically, and we intend to begin clinical testing and generate early clinical data with SG293 in certain B cell cancers as early as this year. For additional information, see the section titled "T Cell-Targeted Fusosome Approach" below.

Previously, we were also pursuing programs in the field of HIP-edited ex vivo CAR T therapy. However, in order to prioritize development of our SC451 and SG293 programs, in November 2025, we announced our decision to suspend development of our allogeneic CAR T programs, including SC291 and SC262, and to halt further enrollment in the Phase 1 GLEAM and VIVID trials of these candidates. While the allogeneic CAR T programs increased our confidence in our HIP platform, we believe the impact we can have for patients and shareholders is now greater with increased focus on SC451 and SG293.

Risks Related to the Development and Clinical Testing of Our Product Candidates
paragraphs: Investing in shares of our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the following risks and uncertainties, together with all of the other information contained in this Annual Report, including our financial statements and related notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report, before making an investment decision. The risks described below are not the only ones we face. Many of the following risks and uncertainties are, and will continue to be, exacerbated by any worsening of the global geo-political, business, and economic environment. The occurrence of any of the following risks, or of additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial, could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, reputation, or results of operations. In such a case, the trading price of shares of our common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment.

Our ex vivo and in vivo cell engineering platforms are based on novel technologies that are unproven and may not result in approvable or marketable products. This uncertainty exposes us to unforeseen risks, makes it difficult for us to predict the time and cost that will be required for the development and potential regulatory approval of our product candidates, and increases the risk that we may ultimately not be successful in our efforts to use and expand our technology platforms to build a pipeline of product candidates.

A key element of our strategy is to identify and develop a pipeline of product candidates using our ex vivo and in vivo cell engineering platforms and advance those product candidates through clinical development for the treatment of various different diseases. The scientific research that forms the basis of our efforts to develop product candidates with our platforms is still ongoing. We are not aware of any FDA-approved therapeutics that are cell products derived from pluripotent stem cells (PSCs) or that utilize our fusogen technology. Further, the scientific evidence that supports the feasibility of developing therapeutic treatments based on our platforms is preliminary, limited, and remains ongoing. We are therefore exposed to a number of unforeseen risks, and it is difficult to predict the types of challenges and risks that we may encounter during development of our product candidates.

Preclinical and clinical testing of product candidates is inherently unpredictable and may lead to unexpected results, in particular when such product candidates are based on novel technologies. For example, we have not tested our cell engineering platforms on all cell types or in all microenvironments, and results from one cell type or microenvironment may not translate into other cell types or microenvironments. In addition, our current gene editing approaches rely on novel gene editing reagents that may have unanticipated or undesirable effects or prove to be less effective than we expect. Also, we are in the early stages of testing product candidates developed using our cell engineering platforms in humans, and most of our current data are limited to animal models and preclinical cell lines and assays, which may not accurately predict the safety and efficacy of our product candidates in humans. Additionally, we and third parties may have limited preclinical and clinical data, and a more limited understanding generally, with respect to certain indications, such as autoimmune diseases, and we cannot predict the extent to which the safety and efficacy of a product candidate may vary across indications. We may encounter significant challenges creating appropriate models and assays for evaluating the safety and purity of our product candidates and may not be able to provide sufficient data or other evidence, to the satisfaction of regulatory authorities, that certain unexpected results observed in preclinical and clinical testing of our product candidates are not indicative of the potential safety issues of such product candidates. In addition, we may use manufacturing reagents and materials across various programs and initiatives. Certain reagents and materials may be novel and have unknown or unanticipated effects, including with respect to a product candidate's safety, efficacy, or manufacturability. Any unanticipated or adverse effects related or attributed to such reagents or materials could affect all the programs and initiatives in which they are used, and result in delays and harm our ability to timely and successfully progress our product candidates through preclinical and clinical development.

We may develop program plans and timelines for certain product candidates based on our experience with such product candidates in different indications or with other product candidates that incorporate or were developed with the same technologies based on our expectation that such product candidates will perform and act similarly. However, our product candidates may reveal unexpected, important differences, including with respect to safety or efficacy, when developed in different indications or as compared to such other product candidates, including differences that may require changes to the manufacturing process or clinical development plan that require additional time and resources beyond what we initially anticipated. Any such occurrence could require us to adjust or alter our development plans, which could delay, harm, or prevent our ability to develop and commercialize such product candidates.

In addition, product candidates developed with our hypoimmune and fusogen technologies have potential safety risks, including those related to genotoxicity associated with the delivery of genome-modifying payloads. For example, DNA sequences that randomly integrate into a cell's DNA may increase the risk for or cause certain cancers. Additionally, gene editing approaches may edit the genome at sites other than the intended DNA target or cause DNA rearrangements, each of which may have oncogenic or other adverse effects. PSC-derived cell products may have potential safety risks related to genomic and epigenomic variations that have occurred or may occur during the manufacturing process. We cannot always predict the types and potential impact of these genomic changes, including whether certain changes are or may eventually be harmful. Accordingly, it may be difficult for us to conduct the level of testing and assay development necessary to ensure that our PSC-derived cell product candidates have an acceptable safety profile when used in humans. These risks related to genetic variation are also relevant to any product candidates we may develop using donor-derived cells. Additionally, our stem cell-based product candidates have potential safety risks that may result from cells that are undifferentiated or have not been completely differentiated to the desired phenotype and lead to oncogenic transformations or other adverse effects. As a result, it is possible that safety events or concerns could negatively affect the development of our product candidates, as described elsewhere in these Risk Factors.

We believe the time is right to develop engineered cell therapies in various therapeutic areas. Substantial progress in the understanding of genetics, gene editing, protein engineering, stem cell biology, immunology, process analytics, and computational biology have converged to create an opportunity to markedly increase the breadth and depth of the potential impact of cellular medicines. We continue to make progress developing our ex vivo cell engineering platform that leverages our HIP technology and our in vivo cell engineering platform. We continue to make progress on advancing our product candidates into and through preclinical development and toward potential IND submissions. As our product candidates advance toward potential IND submissions, we are conducting good laboratory practices toxicology studies and establishing necessary scale-up for our manufacturing processes.

We expect to continue to assess and prioritize our programs on an ongoing basis based on various factors, including internal and external opportunities and constraints, which may result in our decision to advance certain programs ahead or instead of others or suspend, discontinue, or divest certain programs that represent our current development focus. For details regarding our product candidates, see the section titled "Business—Overview" in Part I, Item 1 included elsewhere in this Annual Report.

Our ex vivo and in vivo technologies represent an aggregation of years of innovation and technology from multiple academic institutions and companies, including hypoimmune technology licensed from the President and Fellows of Harvard College (Harvard) and The Regents of the University of California, fusogen technology acquired from Cobalt Biomedicine Inc. (Cobalt), and gene editing technology licensed from Beam Therapeutics Inc. (Beam), among others. For details regarding these acquisitions and license and collaboration agreements, see Note 4, Acquisitions and Note 5, License and collaboration agreements, to our consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report, as well as the section titled "Business—Key Intellectual Property Agreements" in Part I, Item 1 included elsewhere in this Annual Report.

Our operations to date have included developing our ex vivo and in vivo cell engineering platforms, identifying and developing potential product candidates, executing preclinical studies, establishing manufacturing capabilities, conducting clinical trials of our product candidates, supporting clinical trials of product candidates developed using our technologies, acquiring technologies, staffing the company, business planning, establishing and maintaining our intellectual property portfolio, raising capital, and providing general and administrative support for these operations. All of our programs are currently in the development stage, and we do not have any products approved for sale. We have incurred net losses each year since our inception. Our net losses for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023 were $244.2 million, $266.8 million, and $283.3 million, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $1.8 billion. Our net losses resulted primarily from our research and development programs, and, to a lesser extent, general and administrative costs associated with our operations.

paragraphs: 本公司成立的理念是，工程化細胞將成為未來數十年內醫學最重要的轉變之一。可以透過工程化細胞從根本上解決的疾病負擔相當重大。本公司認為工程化細胞具有與生物藥物一樣顛覆臨牀實踐的潛力，使我們能夠在必要時修復體內細胞，或在需要時替換它們。本公司已開發出體外與體內細胞工程平台，以革新治療範圍廣泛的未滿足治療需求的疾病，包括第一型糖尿病、腫瘤學以及B細胞介導的自身免疫疾病。

針對我們的體外平台，我們已專注投資於我們稱為HIP技術的 hypoimmune 平台技術，目標是工程化能夠「隱藏」在患者免疫系統之外的異體細胞，以克服免疫排斥與細胞持續性的根本挑戰，並能大規模製造。成功的治療需要細胞能夠植入、功能正常並在體內持續存在，我們認為我們的方法可以啟動一連串顛覆性的治療方式，從第一型糖尿病開始。針對體內治療，旨在修復或控制體內基因，成功的產品候選藥物需要基因改造與體內遞送治療載體。我們的初步重點在於將遺傳載體，稱為嵌合抗原受體（CARs），專門遞送到患者的T細胞，產生並增殖CAR T細胞，這些細胞已被證明能減少患者的致病B細胞。
本公司目前專注於推進兩種不同的治療方式，每種都利用其中一種平台技術。SC451 是我們 HIP 編輯的產品候選藥物，用於治療第一型糖尿病。SG293 是我們的體內 CAR T 產品候選藥物，用於治療 B 細胞惡性腫瘤和 B 細胞介導的自身免疫疾病。

• 第一型糖尿病：全球約有十萬人患有第一型糖尿病（T1D），自一百多年前發現胰島素注射以來，對此疾病的治療進展有限。我們正在開發 SC451，一種 HIP 編輯的、來自幹細胞的胰島細胞治療方式，用於治療 T1D。此治療的目標是達到正常的血糖水平，而不需要外源性胰島素注射或免疫抑制。透過一項第一個在人體進行的 investigator-sponsored study（IST），我們已顯示 UP421，一種使用我們 HIP 技術工程化的異體原生胰島細胞治療方式，可以在 T1D 患者移植後十二個月內存活並發揮功能，而不需要免疫抑制。我們已將此 HIP 技術整合至更可擴充的製造平台中，並預計在這一年內提交新藥申請（IND）並開始此治療方式的第一期臨牀試驗。

• 體內 CAR T 細胞：利用我們的 fusogen 平台，該平台可實現細胞專門的體內遞送各種載體，我們正在開發 SG293，一種 CD8 細胞靶向的 fusosome。SG293 將遺傳材料遞送到 CD8+ T 細胞，使其成為 CD19 細胞靶向的 CAR T 細胞，同時避免可能對肝臟和性腺等組織造成問題的遞送。體內 CAR T 細胞有潛力提供與自體、體外製造的 CAR T 細胞一樣的臨牀效益，同時避免需要淋巴清除化療以及製造過程中的複雜性與延遲。SG293 建立在我們先前主要的體內 CAR T 產品候選藥物 SG299 的數據之上。我們計畫在一系列 B 細胞癌與 B 細胞介導的自身免疫疾病中開發 SG293，並預計在這一年內產生初步的臨牀數據。

SC451 是我們針對第一型糖尿病的主要計畫。第一型糖尿病是一種患者的免疫系統攻擊並殺死患者的胰島 β 細胞，這是人體唯一製造胰島素的細胞，導致受影響者完全失去胰島素製造能力的疾病。胰島素對正常的細胞代謝至關重要，而在一百多年前發現胰島素替代治療之前，患者通常在診斷後數個月內死亡。胰島素治療已顯著改善患者的治療結果，但即使在現今最先進的醫療照護與技術及血糖控制下，患有第一型糖尿病的人壽命仍比無此疾病的人短約十年，並需終生承擔顯著的治療負擔。相較之下，我們的目標是開發一種一次性的治療方式，使患者的血糖水平恢復正常，不需要胰島素注射，也不需要免疫抑制，以期讓患者恢復診斷前的生活方式。胰島由胰島 β 細胞和其他內分泌細胞組成。科學家已顯示移植的胰島可以讓患者停止使用胰島素並維持正常的血糖水平。這些胰島可以來自過世捐贈者或來自幹細胞。然而，這些治療的影響力受到限制，因為患者必須持續接受全身性免疫抑制以防止患者的免疫系統排斥這些移植的細胞。免疫抑制的潛在並發症包括增加感染風險、提高癌症風險、心血管疾病、代謝症候羣、慢性腎臟病以及骨質疏鬆，對大多數患者而言，這些並發症的風險大於這些治療的潛在好處。
我們的 HIP 技術設計用於隱藏移植的細胞，使其不被免疫系統辨識與排斥。除了廣泛的預臨牀測試，我們的 HIP 技術隱藏移植的胰島細胞不被免疫系統辨識與排斥的能力已在人體中得到驗證。

2024 年 12 月，UP421，一種 HIP 編輯的異體原生胰島細胞治療方式，被移植至一名患有第一型糖尿病的患者體內，此研究在烏普薩拉大學醫院進行的 investigator-sponsored study（IST）中進行。此研究評估將 UP421 移植至第一型糖尿病患者肌肉內的安全性。次要評估指標包括免疫逃逸、非空腹 C-肽濃度在週邊血液中的表現、混合餐耐受測試（MMTT）後的 C-肽反應，以及透過磁共振成像（MRI）和正子發射體層攝影（PET/MRI）評估移植器官的存活情況。胰島 β 細胞產生前胰島素，該物質被切割並分泌為胰島素和 C-肽，比例為 1:1，使 C-肽成為內源性胰島素產生的可靠生物指標。42 歲的受試者已患有第一型糖尿病超過 30 年，接受了一次 UP421 移植至前臂肌肉中。移植過程未使用免疫抑制、類固醇或其他支持性藥物以促進異體細胞存活。作為一項第一個在人體進行的研究，主要評估指標為安全性，並給予約通常所需胰島細胞數量的 7% 的劑量。

2025 年 1 月，我們宣佈在細胞移植後四周的 IST 研究中取得正面結果，顯示胰臟 β 細胞的存活與功能，透過循環 C-肽的出現來衡量。2025 年 9 月，IST 的 12 週數據發表於《新英格蘭醫學期刊》。此外，我們最近報告指出，在移植後 12 個月，UP421 首例人體研究持續顯示移植的 HIP 改良原生胰島細胞的耐受性、存活與功能。安全性為主要評估指標，且未報告與藥品相關的不良事件。移植前，C-肽水平在非空腹狀態及 MMTT 後均無法偵測。研究結果顯示，在移植後 12 個月，胰臟 β 細胞的存活與功能透過循環 C-肽的出現來衡量。在這些時間點的測試中，C-肽水平在 MMTT 後也增加，與進食後胰島素分泌一致。12 週及 12 個月的 PET/MRI 影像結果與患者前臂肌肉中的胰臟 β 細胞存活與功能一致。

UP421 藥品包含一組胰島細胞族羣：表現 HLA 類 I 及類 II 的野生型 (WT) 胰島細胞、去除 HLA 類 I 及類 II 的雙敲除 (DKO) 胰島細胞，以及去除 HLA 類 I 及類 II 並過度表現 CD47 的 HIP 胰島細胞。我們進行了測試，評估患者對這些不同細胞族羣的免疫反應。根據移植後異體組織的預期反應，WT 胰島細胞引發強烈的免疫反應，包括 T 細胞殺傷及捐贈者特異性抗體的產生。DKO 胰島細胞雖然避免 T 細胞活化及抗體反應，但被自然殺傷 (NK) 細胞迅速清除。相反地，HIP 胰島細胞顯示全面的免疫逃逸，無 T 細胞活化、捐贈者特異性抗體產生或 NK 細胞殺傷的跡象。這些不同的免疫反應在全血測試中進一步驗證，HIP 胰島細胞在暴露於患者外周血液單核細胞 (PBMCs) 後存活，而 WT 和 DKO 胰島細胞則被清除。這些體外測試結果與目前研究 52 週的結果一致。有關上述遺傳改良的更多資訊，請參閱以下標題為「異體治療的免疫障礙背景與現有限制」、「我們的解決方案 – 假免疫技術」及「設計假免疫細胞」的章節。

據我們所知，這項研究是首例成功移植且不使用免疫抑制劑，於具有完整免疫系統的人體中顯示異體細胞存活與功能的案例。我們認為這些 HIP 改良細胞的結果代表細胞治療領域的重要里程碑。這些細胞不僅必須克服異體細胞的典型排斥，還必須克服對胰臟 β 細胞的預存自身免疫反應。這些結果是我們努力開發 SC451，我們的 HIP 改良來源於幹細胞的胰島細胞產品候選藥物，作為 1 型糖尿病患者的現成細胞治療的重要里程碑。
UP421 來源於已故捐贈者的細胞。相較之下，SC451 來源於幹細胞，因此更適合商業規模生產。我們在過去一年中對 SC451 有顯著進展。我們已完成基因改良幹細胞主細胞庫的製造，開始將 Phase 1 生產流程技術轉移給合作製造商，持續進行必要的臨牀前測試，並與世界各地的監管機構會面。我們預計在本年度內提交 SC451 的 IND 並開始 Phase 1 試驗。

關於我們的體內細胞工程研究，我們已從早期的 SG299 體內 CAR T 候選藥物進步到改進的下一代產品候選藥物 SG293，兩者皆使用我們專利的融合子基質遞送平台。2026 年 1 月，我們分享了一項臨牀前研究的數據，使用 SG293 的替代品，該替代品可遞送 CD20 CAR 以針對非人類靈長類 (NHP) B 細胞，在 cynomolgus macaques 中進行測試。此研究中未給予 NHPs 淋巴清除治療。單次靜脈注射 SG293 替代品至這些 NHPs，導致體內 CAR T 細胞的強烈生成，並在外周血液及淋巴結中造成深度 B 細胞清除。B 細胞清除進一步由淋巴結活檢顯示清除 B 細胞，以及 NHPs 的 B 細胞組合重設為 naïve B 細胞。我們認為在這個臨牀前模型中深度 B 細胞清除是針對 B 細胞癌症及 B 細胞介導的自身免疫疾病的潛在療效最重要的生物指標。另外，使用 SG293 的體外研究顯示選擇性基因遞送至 CD8+ T 細胞，對肝臟及性腺組織等組織的非目標轉導極低或無法偵測，支持 SG293 的特異性。我們持續進行 SG293 的臨牀前評估，並計畫在某些 B 細胞癌症中進行臨牀測試，產生早期臨牀數據，預計在本年度內進行。有關更多資訊，請參閱以下標題為「T 細胞靶向融合子方法」的章節。

先前，我們也在 HIP 編輯的體外 CAR T 治療領域進行過計畫。然而，為了優先發展 SC451 和 SG293 計畫，我們在 2025 年 11 月宣佈決定暫停開發我們的異體 CAR T 計畫，包括 SC291 和 SC262，並停止這些候選藥物的 Phase 1 GLEAM 和 VIVID 試驗進一步納入受試者。雖然異體 CAR T 計畫提高了我們對 HIP 平台的信心，但我們認為現在將更多資源集中在 SC451 和 SG293 上，對患者和股東的影響更大。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之分析，並與我們經審計之合併財務報表及相關附註說明一併參考。本討論與分析及其他部分之本年度報告包含前瞻性陳述，這些陳述係基於目前信念、計畫與對未來事件及我們未來財務表現之預期，涉及風險、不確定性與假設，例如有關我們意圖、計畫、目標與對業務之預期之陳述。我們實際結果及部分事件之時程可能與這些前瞻性陳述所描述或暗示者有重大差異，原因包括本年度報告中標題為「風險因素」之部分所列因素。請參閱本年度報告中標題為「關於前瞻性陳述之特別說明」之部分。
我們成立之初，相信工程細胞將是未來數十年內醫學最重要的變革之一。能從根本原因處理之疾病負擔相當重大。我們認為工程細胞有潛力如同生物藥物一樣，對臨牀實務造成顛覆性影響，使我們能根據需要修復體內細胞或更換細胞。我們已發展出體外與體內細胞工程平台，以革新治療多種未滿足治療需求之療效領域，包括第一型糖尿病、腫瘤學與B細胞媒介之自身免疫疾病。

針對我們之體外平台，我們已針對我們所稱為HIP技術之 hypoimmune 平台技術進行專注投資，目標為工程能「隱藏」於患者免疫系統之外之異體細胞，以克服免疫排斥與細胞持續性之根本挑戰，並能大規模製造。成功的治療需要細胞能在體內植入、功能正常且持續存在，我們相信我們的方案能啟動一連串顛覆性治療，從第一型糖尿病開始。針對體內治療，旨在修復或控制體內基因之產品，成功的產品候選者需要基因改造與體內遞送治療載體。我們的初步重點為將遺傳載體，稱為嵌合抗原受體（CARs），專門遞送至患者之T細胞，產生並增殖CAR T細胞，這些細胞已被證明能減少患者之致病B細胞。
我們目前專注於推進兩種不同的治療方案，每種均運用其中一種平台技術。SC451為我們用HIP技術修改之治療第一型糖尿病之產品候選品。SG293為我們用於治療B細胞惡性腫瘤與B細胞媒介之自身免疫疾病的體內CAR T產品候選品。我們保留這些產品候選品之全球權利。

• 第一型糖尿病：全球約有十萬人受第一型糖尿病（T1D）所苦，自一百多年前胰島素注射問世以來，對此疾病的治療進展有限。我們正在開發SC451，一種經HIP技術修改、由幹細胞衍生之胰島細胞治療，用於治療T1D。此治療之目標為達到正常血糖（euglycemia），即無需外源性胰島素注射或免疫抑制。透過一項首次人體研究（IST），我們已顯示UP421，一種經HIP技術工程化之異體原始胰島細胞治療，可在T1D患者移植後十二個月內存活並發揮功能，且無需免疫抑制。我們已將此HIP技術整合至更可擴充製造之平台SC451，並預計於今年內提交新藥申請（IND）並開始此治療之第一期臨牀試驗。

• 體內CAR T細胞：運用我們之融合素平台，該平台可實現細胞專門化、體內遞送各種載體，我們正在開發SG293，一種CD8目標之融合囊泡。SG293將遺傳材料遞送至CD8+ T細胞，使其轉變為CD19目標之CAR T細胞，同時避免對肝臟與生殖腺等組織造成潛在問題之遞送。體內CAR T細胞有潛力提供與自體、體外製造之CAR T細胞相同之臨牀效益，同時避免淋巴清除化療之需求，以及製造過程中的重大複雜性與瓶頸。SG293建立於我們先前領先之體內CAR T產品候選品SG299之數據。我們計畫在多種B細胞癌症與B細胞媒介之自身免疫疾病中開發SG293，並預計於今年內產生初步臨牀數據。
2025年11月，為優先配置資源並追求SC451與融合素計畫之有前景數據，我們宣佈優先發展SC451與SG293計畫，並暫停開發我們兩種異體細胞治療CAR T計畫 – SC291用於B細胞媒介之自身免疫疾病與SC262用於腫瘤學。作為這些努力之一環，我們正在終結評估SC291在B細胞媒介之自身免疫疾病之GLEAM第一期臨牀試驗與評估SC262在腫瘤學之VIVID第一期臨牀試驗。
我們認為現在正是發展工程細胞治療各療效領域之時機。遺傳學、基因編輯、蛋白質工程、幹細胞生物學、免疫學、過程分析學與計算生物學之重大進展已匯集，創造出機會大幅增加細胞藥物之潛在影響範圍與深度。我們持續在發展我們之體外細胞工程平台，該平台運用HIP技術與體內細胞工程平台。我們每一項計畫均有潛力提供獨立之重大價值，同時也支持我們未來進一步運用這些平台之潛力，以開發廣泛適用之藥物。

關於我們的 ex vivo 細胞工程努力，在 2026 年 1 月，我們宣佈 UP421 IST 顯示 12 個月的結果，顯示所有主要和次要端點皆達成。該研究顯示沒有與藥品相關的不良事件。此外，有證據顯示移植後 12 個月內，透過正子發射斷層造影與磁共振成像（PET/MRI）以及可偵測的 C-肽產生，顯示移植物存活與功能。C-肽水平在混合餐耐受測試中如預期般增加，顯示移植的胰島細胞適當的功能。免疫學分析顯示 HIP 改良的胰島細胞具有全面的免疫逃逸。在 2025 年 8 月，新英格蘭醫學期刊發表了一篇標題為 "Transplanted Allogeneic Beta Cells Survival with No Immunosuppression" 的期刊文章，討論該試驗的 12 週結果。我們持續進行 SC451 的預臨牀開發，最近的監管互動結果，包括 FDA INTERACT 和 Pre-IND 會議，增加了我們對製造流程、製造控制、非臨牀測試計畫與臨牀試驗計畫的信心。

關於我們的 in vivo 細胞工程研究努力，在 2026 年 1 月，我們分享了一項預臨牀研究的數據，該研究使用 SG293 的替代品，該替代品可傳遞 CD20 CAR，能針對非人類靈長類（NHP）B 細胞，在無淋巴清除的情況下，在 cynomolgus macaques 中進行。將 SG293 替代品單次靜脈注射至這些 NHP 中，導致強烈的 in vivo CAR T 細胞生成，並在週邊血液與淋巴結中造成深層 B 細胞清除。B 細胞清除進一步由淋巴結活檢顯示清除 B 細胞以及 NHP 的 B 細胞 repertoire 向 naïve B 細胞 "重置" 所確認。我們認為，在此預臨牀模型中深層 B 細胞清除是針對 B 細胞癌症與 B 細胞介導的自身免疫疾病的潛在療效最重要的生物指標。另外，使用 SG293 進行的體外研究顯示選擇性基因傳遞至 CD8+ T 細胞，並在肝臟與生殖腺等組織中顯示極少或無法偵測的離標轉導，支持 SG293 的專一性。
我們持續在預臨牀開發階段推進我們的產品候選品，並朝向潛在的 IND 提交。隨著我們的產品候選品朝向潛在的 IND 提交，我們正在進行良好實驗室實踐（GLP）毒理學研究，並建立我們製造流程所需的規模擴張。
我們預期會持續根據各種因素，包括內部與外部的機會與限制，評估並優先處理我們的計畫。這可能導致我們決定加速某些計畫的進行，或取代其他計畫，或暫停、終止或出售某些計畫，這些計畫代表我們目前的開發重點。有關我們產品候選品的詳細資訊，請參閱本年度報告中「業務—概覽」部分，位於第一部分，項目 1 的內容。

我們的 ex vivo 與 in vivo 技術代表多年來自多個學術機構與公司的創新與技術整合，包括從哈佛大學（Harvard）與加州大學（The Regents of the University of California）取得的 hypoimmune 技術，從 Cobalt Biomedicine Inc.（Cobalt）取得的 fusogen 技術，以及從 Beam Therapeutics Inc.（Beam）取得的基因編輯技術，以及其他技術。有關這些收購與授權與合作協議的詳細資訊，請參閱本年度報告中我們合併財務報表的附註 4，收購，以及附註 5，授權與合作協議，以及本年度報告中「業務—關鍵智慧財產權協議」部分，位於第一部分，項目 1 的內容。

我們至今的運作包括發展我們的 ex vivo 與 in vivo 細胞工程平台、識別與開發潛在產品候選品、執行預臨牀研究、建立製造能力、進行我們產品候選品的臨牀試驗、支持使用我們技術開發的產品候選品的臨牀試驗、取得技術、組建公司團隊、業務規劃、建立與維護我們的智慧財產權組合、籌集資金，以及為這些運作提供一般及行政支援。我們所有的計畫目前都處於開發階段，我們目前沒有任何已核准銷售的產品。我們自成立以來每年都產生淨虧損。我們在 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日與 2023 年 12 月 31 日的淨虧損分別為 244.2 百萬美元、266.8 百萬美元與 283.3 百萬美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們累計虧損為 1.8 十億美元。我們的淨虧損主要來自我們的研究與開發計畫，以及較少程度的與我們運作相關的一般及行政費用。

headings: 與本公司及產業相關之風險
我們可能無法實現所取得或已授權，或未來將取得或授權之技術之效益。
本公司開發細胞工程平台及產品候選藥物之能力，以及未來成長，皆依賴於留住關鍵人才並招募更多合格人才。
若本公司擴展營運，包括開發及監管能力，可能遭遇管理成長之困難，此等困難可能幹擾本公司營運，並對本公司業務造成其他損害。
與產品候選藥物之開發及臨牀測試相關之風險
paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股股份涉及高度風險。您應仔細考慮下列風險與不確定性，並配合本年度報告中所有其他資訊，包括財務報表及相關附註，以做出投資決定。下列所描述的風險並非我們唯一面臨的風險。許多下列風險與不確定性，將因全球地緣政治、商業與經濟環境惡化而更加嚴重。任何下列風險發生，或出現目前未為我們所知或我們認為不重要之其他風險與不確定性，均可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、聲譽或營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。在此情況下，本公司普通股股份的交易價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。
我們的 ex vivo 與 in vivo 細胞工程平台基於創新技術，尚未經證實，可能無法產生可批准或可市場化的產品。此不確定性使我們面臨未預見的風險，使我們難以預測開發產品候選藥物及潛在監管批准所需時間與成本，並增加我們最終可能無法成功運用並擴展技術平台以建立產品候選藥物產品線的風險。

我們策略的重要組成部分是透過 ex vivo 與 in vivo 細胞工程平台識別與開發產品候選藥物，並推動這些產品候選藥物進行臨牀開發，以治療各種不同的疾病。我們開發產品候選藥物的科學研究仍處於進行中。我們尚未知悉任何美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准的療法為來自多能幹細胞（PSCs）的細胞製品，或使用我們的融合素技術。此外，支持我們平台開發治療性療法可行性的科學證據仍屬初步、有限且持續進行中。因此，我們面臨許多未預見的風險，且難以預測在開發產品候選藥物過程中可能遇到的挑戰與風險類型。

產品候選藥物的預臨牀與臨牀測試本質上難以預測，可能導致意外結果，特別是在這些產品候選藥物基於創新技術的情況下。例如，我們尚未在所有細胞類型或微環境中測試我們的細胞工程平台，且某一細胞類型或微環境的結果可能無法轉移到其他細胞類型或微環境。此外，我們目前的基因編輯方法依賴創新基因編輯試劑，這些試劑可能產生未預見或不理想的影響，或證明其效果不如我們預期。另外，我們在人類身上測試使用我們細胞工程平台開發的產品候選藥物仍處於早期階段，且目前大多數數據僅限於動物模型與預臨牀細胞株與試驗，可能無法準確預測產品候選藥物在人類中的安全性與有效性。此外，我們與第三方可能對某些適應症（如自身免疫疾病）的預臨牀與臨牀數據有限，且對此類適應症的瞭解一般也較有限，我們無法預測產品候選藥物在不同適應症中的安全性與有效性可能有多大差異。我們可能面臨創建適當模型與試驗以評估產品候選藥物安全性與純度的挑戰，且可能無法提供足夠的數據或其他證據，以符合監管機構的要求，使某些預臨牀與臨牀測試中觀察到的意外結果不反映產品候選藥物的潛在安全性問題。此外，我們可能在不同計畫與專案中使用製造試劑與材料。某些試劑與材料可能為創新，且其影響未知或未預見，包括對產品候選藥物安全性、有效性或製造可行性之影響。任何未預見或不利的影響與試劑或材料相關或歸因於這些試劑或材料，可能影響所有使用這些試劑或材料的計畫與專案，並導致延誤，影響我們及時且成功地推動產品候選藥物通過預臨牀與臨牀開發的能力。

我們可能根據我們在不同適應症中或與其他使用相同技術開發的產品候選藥物的經驗，為某些產品候選藥物制定計畫與時間表。然而，產品候選藥物在不同適應症中開發或與其他產品候選藥物比較時，可能顯示出未預見的重要差異，包括安全性或有效性方面，這些差異可能需要修改製造過程或臨牀開發計畫，而這些修改可能需要超出我們最初預期的額外時間與資源。任何此類情況都可能導致我們調整或改變開發計畫，這可能延誤、損害或阻止我們開發與商業化這些產品候選藥物的能力。

此外，使用我們的 hypoimmune 與 fusogen 技術開發的產品候選藥物可能具有潛在的安全風險，包括與基因組修改載荷傳遞相關的基因毒性。例如，隨機整合至細胞 DNA 的 DNA 序列可能增加某些癌症的風險或導致癌症。此外，基因編輯方法可能在非預期的 DNA 目標位點進行編輯，或導致 DNA 重組，這可能產生致癌或其它不良影響。來自 PSC 的細胞製品可能因製造過程中的基因組與表觀基因組變異而具有潛在的安全風險。我們無法總是預測這些基因組變異的類型與潛在影響，包括某些變異是否為有害或最終可能有害。因此，我們可能難以進行足夠的測試與試驗開發，以確保我們的 PSC 來源細胞產品候選藥物在人類使用時具有可接受的安全性。這些與基因變異相關的風險也適用於我們可能使用捐贈者來源細胞開發的任何產品候選藥物。此外，我們的幹細胞基產品候選藥物可能因未分化或未完全分化至目標表型的細胞而產生潛在的安全風險，導致致癌轉變或其他不良影響。因此，安全性事件或問題可能對我們產品候選藥物的開發產生負面影響，如本風險因素中其他部分所述。
